examples.knowledge_point: Projecting a Vector Onto a Perpendicular Vector
examples.problem: Let $[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ and $[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -4 \\ 0\end{aligned}]$ Find the scalar projection of $\mathbf{a}$ onto $\mathbf{b}.$
examples.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the scalar projection, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{comp}}_{b}\,a & =\frac{a\cdot b}{|\,b\,|} \\  & =\frac{{a}_{x}{b}_{x}+{a}_{y}{b}_{y}+{c}_{z}{b}_{z}}{\sqrt{{b}_{x}^{2}+{b}_{y}^{2}+{b}_{z}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{0\cdot 2+0\cdot (-4)+1\cdot 0}{\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(-4)^{2}+{0}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{0}{\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(-4)^{2}+{0}^{2}}} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem: Let $a=⟨3,2,1⟩$ and $b=⟨3,4,1⟩.$ Find the scalar projection of $a$ onto $b.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the scalar projection, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{comp}}_{b}\,a & =\frac{a\cdot b}{|\,b\,|} \\  & =\frac{{a}_{x}{b}_{x}+{a}_{y}{b}_{y}+{a}_{z}{b}_{z}}{\sqrt{{b}_{x}^{2}+{b}_{y}^{2}+{b}_{z}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{3\cdot 3+2\cdot 4+1\cdot 1}{\sqrt{{3}^{2}+{4}^{2}+{1}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{18}{\sqrt{26}}.\end{aligned}
$$
